# Fate UI v0.8.9-beta1

This beta adds a multi-folder workspace, durable session tasks, and a larger Agent Teams V2 lifecycle. It also changes normal launches to reuse the running Fate UI process.

## Multi-folder workspace

- Keeps several project folders in one sidebar, with sessions grouped under each folder.
- Lets you focus a known folder, inspect its saved sessions, reveal it on disk, or remove its saved sessions without opening another app window.
- Keeps active Pi work running when you move to another folder. Fate UI reuses live project runtimes and removes idle runtimes after a grace period.
- Adds compact session rows for people who keep many folders and conversations open.
- Remembers the last trusted project and restores it on a normal desktop launch.

## Session tasks and GoalMax

- Adds durable, session-scoped task lists with create, update, reorder, delete, and clear actions.
- Shows the current task above the conversation and keeps task state tied to its project and session.
- Mirrors active GoalMax criteria into the task list. Required work stays behind the completion gate until current evidence and independent verification agree.
- Holds follow-up prompts while GoalMax verification or context compaction is still active, then releases them through the normal queue.

## Agent Teams V2

- Supports several named teams in one root session, with explicit create, select, pause, resume, reset, close, and release controls.
- Adds queue and steer delivery modes for messages to active children.
- Keeps closed team history while release frees runtime capacity and writer leases.
- Enforces one project writer across teams, so two teams cannot write to the same working tree at the same time.
- Expands the inspector and session panels for team status, lifecycle actions, usage, and retained history.

## Browser and desktop behavior

- Remembers the last HTTP or HTTPS page for each project in the built-in browser.
- Runs one Fate UI process by default. A later `fate <folder>` command focuses the running app and opens that folder. Use `--new-instance` when you need a separate process and profile.
- Fixes early second-launch handling and resolves relative project paths from the terminal that launched them.
- Keeps task events connected when the focused project runtime changes.
- Updates the application icon artwork and platform-specific icon spacing.

## Compatibility and installers

Existing projects, Pi sessions, settings, themes, and Agent Team history do not need a manual migration. The new task data is stored under Fate UI's local data directory.

GitHub Actions builds and tests this release on Windows x64, macOS Apple Silicon, macOS Intel, and Linux x64. The prerelease contains seven installers plus `SHA256SUMS`:

- Windows x64: NSIS `.exe`
- macOS arm64 and x64: `.dmg` and `.pkg`
- Linux x64: `.AppImage` and `.deb`

Public beta installers remain unsigned. Windows SmartScreen or macOS Gatekeeper may show an unknown-publisher warning. Verify downloads against `SHA256SUMS`.
